questions.qtext:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about variable elimination?
S1 : Selecting an optimal elimination order in variable elimination minimizes network variable.
S2 : Selecting an optimal elimination order in variable elimination minimizes intermediate factor size.

options.text: Only S1
Only S2
Both S1 and S2
None of these

questions.solution:
(b)
S1 : Variable elimination does not change the number of variable in the original network structure.
So, S1 is false.
S2 : The optimal elimination order aims to reduce the size of intermediate factor generated during the elimination process, which improves computational efficiency.

questions.qtext: Which of the following best describes the process of “summing out” a variable in Bayesian network?

options.text: Setting the variable to its observed value in the network.
Adding up the probabilities of all possible value of the variable.
Multiplying the factors involving the variable and them marginalizing over it.
Removing the variable from the network structure.

questions.solution:
(c)
“Summing out” a variable in Bayesian network involves multiplying the relevant conditional
probability distributions and then marginalizing over to compute marginal probabilities efficiently.

In a Bayesian network, the impact of an optimal elimination order.
(a) It reduces the accuracy of the final inference result.
(b) It minimized the number of variable in the network.
(c) It reduces the size of the largest intermediate factors created during the elimination process.
(d) It reduce the size of the initial factors.

options.text: a
b
c
d

questions.solution:

An optimal elimination order minimize the size of the largest intermediate factors formed during variable elimination, reducing computational complexity and memory usage.

questions.qtext: Which of the following is NOT a type of sampling method used for approximate inference?

options.text: Importance Sampling
Gibbs Sampling
Rejection Sampling
Dijkstra Sampling

questions.solution:
(d)
• This method is used in approximate inference to estimate properties of a target distribution by sampling from a proposal distribution.
• This method is used in Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods for approximate
inference, particularly in Bayesian statistics, to sample from high-dimensional distributions.
• This method generates samples from a proposal distribution and filters them based on acceptance criteria defined by the target distribution.
• Dijkstra’s algorithm is a graph search algorithm, not a statistical sampling method used in approximate inference.

questions.qtext:
Which of the following statement is/are correct?
S1 : Likelihood function can be used to directly estimate the parameters of a statistical model.
S2: Rejection sampling requires knowledge of the exact shape of the posterior distribution.

options.text: Only S1
Only S2
Both S1 and S2
Neither S1 nor S2

questions.solution:
(a)
S1 : The likelihood function can indeed be used to estimate the parameters of a statistical model by finding the set of parameters that maximize the likelihood of the observed data. So option S1 is correct.
S2: Rejection sampling does not require knowledge of the exact shape of the posterior distribution. It requires a proposal distribution and can generate samples from the target distribution without needing to know its exact shape. So option S2 is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is correct about the use of the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) method in approximate inference?

options.text: HMC does not use gradient information from the target distribution.
HMC is less efficient than basic Metropolis-Hastings for high-dimensional spaces.
HMC leverages gradient information to propose samples, improving efficiency in highdimensional spaces.
HMC cannot be used for complex probabilistic models.

questions.solution:
(c)
• HMC specifically uses gradient information to improve sampling efficiency. So option (a) is false.
• HMC is generally more efficient than basic Metropolis-Hastings in high-dimensional spaces.
So option (b) is false.
• HMC uses gradient information to propose samples, making it more efficient in highdimensional spaces than basic Metropolis-Hastings. So option (c) is true.
• HMC is particularly useful for complex probabilistic models. So option (d) is false.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements regarding the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm is correct?

options.text: The acceptance probability in Metropolis-Hastings is always 1.
Metropolis-Hastings can be used to sample from a complex target distribution by accepting or rejecting proposed samples based on their likelihood ratios.
The Metropolis-Hastings algorithm does not require a proposal distribution.
Metropolis-Hastings cannot be used for approximate inference.

questions.solution:
(b)
• The acceptance probability can be less than 1 and is calculated based on the likelihood ratios of the proposed and current samples. So option (a) is false.
• This is the fundamental mechanism of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm. So option (b) is true.
• A proposal distribution is essential for generating candidate samples in the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm. So option (c) is false.
• Metropolis-Hastings is a widely used method for approximate inference. So option (d) is false.

questions.qtext:
Consider the process of likelihood weighting in approximate Bayesian inference.
(a) Likelihood weighting samples from the prior distribution of variables.
(b) Likelihood weighting assigns weights to samples based on how well they match the observed evidence.
(c) Likelihood weighting always guarantees exact posterior probabilities.
(d) Likelihood weighting is computationally efficient for large Bayesian networks.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.text: a
b
c
d

questions.solution:
(b, d)
• Likelihood weighting samples from the conditional distribution of variables given the observed evidence, not from the prior distribution. So option (a) is incorrect.
• In likelihood weighting, samples are assigned weights proportional to their likelihood under the observed evidence. This allows for estimation of posterior probabilities. So option (b) is correct.
• Likelihood weighting provides an approximation to the posterior distribution, especially useful when exact inference is computationally infeasible. So option (c) is incorrect.
• Likelihood weighting can be computationally efficient compared to other exact methods, especially for large networks. However, it depends on the complexity of the network and the number of samples required. So option (b) is correct.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following is/are correct using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods in approximate inference?

options.text: Exact computation of posterior distributions.
Ability to handle high-dimensional parameter spaces.
Flexibility to model complex posterior distributions.
Guarantee of finding the global optimum.

questions.solution:
(b, c)
• MCMC methods provide approximate solutions to the posterior distribution rather than exact computations. They rely on sampling methods to approximate the distribution. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• MCMC methods are particularly useful in scenarios involving high-dimensional parameter spaces where exact computations or direct sampling methods may not be feasible. So, option (b) is correct.
• MCMC methods are versatile and can handle complex posterior distributions, which makes them widely applicable in Bayesian inference for various models and data types. So, option (c) is correct.
• MCMC methods are stochastic methods and do not guarantee finding the global optimum. They provide samples that approximate the posterior distribution, but the samples may not necessarily represent the global optimum. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
Consider the Gibbs Sampling in approximate inference.
(a) Gibbs Sampling requires the joint distribution of variables to be known.
(b) Gibbs Sampling guarantees convergence to the true posterior distribution.
(c) Gibbs Sampling samples all variables simultaneously in each iteration.
(d) Gibbs Sampling can handle high-dimensional distributions effectively.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.text: a
b
c
d

questions.solution:
(a, d)
• Gibbs Sampling requires knowledge of the joint distribution to sample from the conditional distributions of variables. So, option (a) is correct.
• While Gibbs Sampling is designed to sample from the posterior distribution, convergence to the true posterior depends on factors such as the mixing properties of the sampler and the number of iterations. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Gibbs Sampling updates variables one at a time based on their conditional distributions. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Gibbs Sampling is known for its effectiveness in sampling from high-dimensional distributions by sequentially updating variables. So, option (d) is correct.
